Claire / team — initial sizing attached. Key points from the model-specific allocator and memory calc:

- Baseline unquantized orion-13b-32k (FP16): per-request KV cache + activations ~ 28.4 GB when serving 32k contexts end-to-end; working set with off-heap buffers (batching + prefetch) ~ 40–44 GB.
- FP16 variant usable on A100-80GB with headroom of ~10–15% for safe concurrency; that implies ~3 pods per 120 concurrent sessions assuming efficient batching (we model 20 req/sec per pod with current batching heuristics).
- 4-bit quantized variant (GPTQ-like/LLM.int4 hybrid) reduces the model memory by ~2.8x for parameters and reduces KV cache marginally (~1.3x) — effective working set ~18–20 GB; fits on 48GB class GPUs with extra room for cache headroom.
- Latency impact: quantized int4 path adds ~8–12ms per-token on our kernel path for autoregressive generation; tail latency impact on long context requests tracked primarily by KV cache eviction and prefetching.
- Operational notes: to hit 99th < 180ms, we recommend a staged pool:
  * Primary: 6x 48GB pods (mixed-precision mode) serving short/medium traffic + burst routing to
  * Long-context pool: 4x 80GB pods (FP16) pinned for >8k context sessions (handles KV heavy tails)
  * Fallbacks: A policy to route overflow to quantized 48GB pool with traffic shaping and prompt truncation policies.

Attached CSV: orion_capacity_calc.csv — contains per-variant per-gpu session capacity, cost delta estimates and a conservative rollout schedule for quantization (canary on 5% of traffic, evaluate quality, then 25%, then 100%).

Notes on pricing: committed pool with this split (6x48 + 4x80) maps to our standard Dedicated SKU with reserved monthly commit; mixing 48GB quantized pods reduces committed GPU-hours by ~38% vs all-FP16 baseline. Final numbers in the attached proposal workbook.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Inference Architect, Redwood Inference

Claire / Daniel —

Thanks for the quick review this morning. Summarizing the recommended committed footprint and next steps so procurement and your infra team can action:

1) Recommended committed pool (initial):
   - 6 x 48GB pods (mixed-precision default, handles 80% of traffic)
   - 4 x 80GB pods (FP16, long-context reserved for >8k sessions)
   - Reservation target: 12 months with quarterly quality gates tied to quantization rollouts.

2) Quantization rollout plan (quality-first):
   - Canary: 5% traffic to int4 hybrid variant for short/medium prompts (2 weeks) + automated eval on your probe set.
   - Gradual ramp: 25% after pass, 50% after second gate, hold 2 weeks, then full ramp.
   - Auto-fallback: if quality delta > 2% on probe set at any gate, rollback to FP16 for that route.

3) Operational controls we will enable at go-live:
   - KV-aware routing: long requests pinned to 80GB pool; prewarming for sessions with >8k context; eviction thresholds for KV cache to avoid OOM during spikes.
   - Burst policy: allow short bursts up to 150 concurrent sessions for 2–5 minutes before shedding to fallbacks.
   - Observability: token-level cost, 99/95/50 latency, and per-route quality regression alerts feeding your webhook.

4) Next steps:
   - I'll send the formal proposal workbook (rdw_dedicated_proposal_orion_v1.xlsx) and SOC2 link.
   - Please confirm: (A) 120 is sustained peak (vs burst), (B) you accept the staged quantization cadence and 12-month reservation.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the numbers live.

—Vivek
